The shift code must be unique within one plant.
Shift "%s" is %s hours long — it has to lie between 0 and 24.
The hour of the day: 6.0 is 06:00, 14.5 is 14:30.
A night shift starts at 22:00 and ends at 06:00 the next day. Forget that and the night shift comes out minus sixteen hours long.
Counted back along the chain of handovers. Three shifts or more means work being passed along, not work that is hard.
Work carried over three shifts or more. Work that has rolled five shifts is being passed along, not hard.
Work still open is carried into the next shift with a trail. Where there is no next shift yet, the system writes a warning into the log.
%d items are unfinished with NO next shift to carry them into. Create the next shift and open it, otherwise nobody takes these on.
Work carried over three shifts or more and still unfinished.\n Rolling five shifts does not mean it is hard — it means nobody is taking it on.
It may be left empty. Plenty of things need handing over before they become work orders — insisting on an order first is exactly how they disappear.
items have rolled over three shifts or\n more. Work that rolls five shifts is not hard — it is\n being passed along.

Handed over but nobody has signed for it. It does not block operations — blocking it makes people sign for each other and the signature stops meaning anything — but it has to be visible, because this is the classic excuse when there is a dispute.

Declare the shift pattern first, then generate shifts for a range of days. Opening a shift makes the system capture the plant's state and pull the previous shift's unfinished work across — nothing falls between two shifts.

Three eight-hour shifts, for example: 06:00, 14:00, 22:00. A shift starting at 22:00 ends at 06:00 the next day — the Crosses midnight column turns itself on so that nobody computes a night shift as minus sixteen hours long.

Ordered by severity: nobody having signed for it is the worst, because in a dispute there is no one who took the shift on. Work rolling across several shifts outranks work still open: still open is normal at the end of a shift, rolling three shifts means it is being passed along.

Record even the things that are not yet work orders: a word of advice, something spotted at the end of the shift, something waiting on a contractor's answer. Insisting on an order before anything may be recorded is exactly how they disappear.
One-way handover — handed over but nobody has signed for it. It does not block operations, but this is precisely the classic excuse in a dispute: "that was never handed over to me".

This is a snapshot taken when the shift opened; it is not recomputed when it is opened again later. The point is to record what the person coming on shift saw — recompute it and six months later it shows today's state, and the record loses all its value.
